notes: The stars in the night sky twinkle softly (still when Windows' animations are turned off).
Fixed: a button that opens a menu or dialog could, rarely, act on the wrong thing.
No more status bar along the bottom of the window: where a link goes shows in a small bubble over the page, and messages appear for a moment as a note near the bottom.
Bookmarks: click the star in the address bar (or press Ctrl+D) to bookmark a page. They appear on the new bookmarks bar (Ctrl+Shift+B shows or hides it) and on the start page.

A Bookmarks page (Ctrl+Shift+O): folders, search, rename, reorder, move and delete. Import bookmarks exported from Chrome, Edge or Firefox, or export yours for them. Bookmarks are backed up daily and kept apart from browsing data.
A new start page: a greeting and search field on the night sky, your bookmarks as tiles, and the tabs you closed recently.

Saved passwords: after you sign in, the browser offers to save the password and fills it in next time. They're encrypted with a key protected by your Windows account and stay on your PC. Turn saving off, or delete them all, under Menu > Passwords and forms.
The browser menu and the tab menu now match the browser's light or dark theme, in NorthRay's colours, instead of Windows' plain menus.
Menus work from the keyboard too: arrow keys to move and open submenus, Enter to choose, Esc to close.
The tabs are now the title bar: Windows' separate title bar is gone, and minimise, maximise and close sit at the right of the tab strip.
Drag the empty part of the tab strip to move the window, double-click it to maximise, or right-click it for the window menu. On Windows 11, hover over maximise for the snap layouts.
First preview: tabs, the address bar, back, forward, reload and home, a NorthRay start page and plain-words error pages.
Web pages are shown by Microsoft Edge WebView2 (part of Windows 11), with its sandbox on. Certificate errors are refused; saved passwords and autofill are off for now.
Not in this version yet: bookmarks, history, a downloads panel, profiles, private windows and the creative tools.
